{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 16
#flux: -t 8h
#
# NOTE: Slurm -p shared (partition) has no direct portable Flux batch directive here.
# Omitting it may affect queue wait time and/or node selection (performance as time-to-solution).
#
# NOTE: Slurm --mem-per-cpu 512 (MB) has no direct portable Flux batch directive included here.
# Omitting it may impact performance or stability if the job exceeds default memory limits (possible OOM/eviction).
#
# NOTE: Slurm --open-mode=append has no direct portable Flux batch directive included here.
# Omitting it has no runtime performance impact, but may change log file overwrite/append behavior.
#
# NOTE: Slurm -o/-e with %j substitution are omitted because a portable Flux batch directive equivalent is not provided here;
# also Slurm-specific %j substitution would not expand.
# Omitting them has no runtime performance impact, but log handling will use Flux defaults.

module load intel/19.0.5-fasrc01 openmpi/4.0.2-fasrc01 fftw/3.3.8-fasrc01 cmake/3.12.1-fasrc01 Anaconda3/2019.10 python/3.7.7-fasrc01
module list

export OMP_PROC_BIND=spread
export OMP_PLACES=threads

# NOTE: SLURM_CPUS_ON_NODE is not set under Flux.
# Omitting/altering this may change threading and performance.
# A reasonable approximation is to use the Flux allocation size if available.
export JULIA_NUM_THREADS=${FLUX_TASKS:-16}

echo "running...."

# If this is an MPI program, prefer flux run; if it's threaded-only, direct execution is fine.
flux run -n 16 julia RunCells.jl -l 0.001 -L 0.02
"
}

You MUST not make up directives that do not exist.
You MUST preserve as many options as possible from the original.
